packet.endpoint_definition: Compare the later working answer with what still limits or could reopen it.

Preserve the speaker's own desire, counterpressure, uncertainty, leaning, commitment, and conditional willingness without flattening or upgrading them.

focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	Our city museum is free, and a popular exhibition has made weekend entry miserable.
e002	People stand outside for an hour, galleries become crowded, and sometimes staff close a room without warning because the safe limit has been reached.
e003	The obvious operational answer is timed entry.
e004	The problem is that our public includes tourists who decide at the door, older residents who do not book online, families whose bus or child does not respect a fifteen-minute slot, and people who cannot wait outside even under the current system.
e005	Staff want predictability.
e006	Some trustees want photographs without queues.
e007	I want fewer unsafe closures and less wasted time, but I do not want a free museum to become technically free and practically available only to people who plan, have a device, and arrive exactly when instructed.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e008	Treat predictable flow and spontaneous access as separate service goals.
e009	Preserve walk-in capacity, non-online booking, flexible arrival, and help at the door.
e010	Measure waiting, closures, unused slots, turn-aways, workload, and who can actually use each path.
[Turn 2 USER]
e011	And please do not treat the current queue as open access.
e012	It favors people who can stand outside.
e013	School groups leave.
e014	Galleries close without warning.
e015	Timed entry can exclude people, but the status quo already does.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e016	Agreed.
e017	Record current waits, turn-aways, abandoned visits, and closures by time and visitor type before the change.
e018	The goal is not to preserve an unmeasured queue.
e019	A pilot can test whether reservations reduce those burdens while ensuring that people without advance plans retain a workable route into the exhibition.
[Turn 3 USER]
e020	Staff designed a ten-week weekend trial.
e021	Forty percent of each hour remains for walk-ins.
e022	Reservations can be made online, by phone, or at the admissions desk up to a week ahead.
e023	Tickets are free, no account is required, and a reservation remains valid for a thirty-minute arrival window.
e024	Unused reserved spaces return to the walk-in pool after that window.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e025	That protects several access modes and limits the penalty for imperfect timing.
e026	Test the phone and desk paths under real demand, make the walk-in allocation visible, and avoid releasing all returned capacity through the online channel.
e027	Decide how school and community groups fit without allowing block bookings to consume the public allotment.
[Turn 4 USER]
e028	Schools keep their existing group process and do not draw from public slots.
e029	Neighborhood organizations asked for a small weekly block they can book by phone for residents who need assistance.
e030	We agreed, but one trustee called that preferential treatment.
e031	I see it as making the channel usable, not giving people better access than everyone else.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e032	Assisted booking can correct a channel barrier if the admission opportunity remains comparable.
e033	Publish the size and purpose of the block, review whether it is used, and release unused places.
e034	The relevant question is whether people can exercise the same public entitlement, not whether every route has identical mechanics.
[Turn 5 USER]
e035	The ticketing provider needs a name and contact method to send the reservation.
e036	It will delete identifiable records after fourteen days and provide only aggregate attendance data to the museum.
e037	Staff will offer anonymous paper walk-in tickets.
e038	We are not connecting reservation history to memberships or donations, and the provider cannot market to visitors.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e039	The data use is proportionate to the booking task.
e040	Verify deletion, minimize what appears on staff screens, and explain the distinction between a reservation record and anonymous walk-in entry.
e041	Keep donor and membership systems technically separate, not merely governed by a promise that the data will not be interesting later.
[Turn 6 USER]
e042	We set review conditions before launch: fewer unplanned gallery closures, shorter waits for both reserved and walk-in visitors, no increase in total turn-aways, acceptable staff workload, and no material access or privacy problem.
e043	Weekly results will be published.
e044	If walk-in turn-aways increase for two weekends, we raise the walk-in share immediately while the trial continues.
e045	The provider contract ends automatically after ten weeks unless the board approves another term.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e046	Those conditions let the operation adapt without converting every adjustment into failure.
e047	Predefine how waits and turn-aways are counted, including people who leave before reaching the desk.
e048	The automatic contract end prevents passive continuation, and public weekly results make it harder to redefine success after seeing which channel performs best.
[Turn 7 USER]
e049	I will recommend the ten-week weekend trial with the forty-percent walk-in floor, phone and desk booking, assisted community access, flexible arrival window, anonymous walk-in tickets, published results, and the early adjustment rule.
e050	We will not change weekday entry or other galleries.
e051	The board review will decide whether timed entry solved more access problems than it created, rather than whether the exhibition looked orderly in photographs.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e052	The proposal is ready as a narrow, observable trial.
e053	It compares the booking system with the actual unequal queue, not an idealized open door.
e054	Walk-in space remains throughout; phone, desk, and assisted booking reduce channel dependence; privacy is limited; and access failures can change the allocation before the final board review.
e055	Execute the counting method as written, especially abandoned visits and walk-in turn-aways, and record any protocol change.
e056	The board should see the complete access pattern rather than reservation volume or photographs of orderly galleries.
[Turn 8 USER]
e057	The baseline broke our categories.
e058	Many “walk-ins” had checked social media that morning and travelled specifically for the exhibition; they just had not made a reservation.
e059	Some tourists were perfectly willing to return later if the time was reliable.
e060	Others could enter only now.
e061	We had built the plan as if reservation meant planned and walk-in meant spontaneous.
e062	That is administratively convenient and behaviorally wrong.
e063	It matters because the forty-percent floor might protect a ticket type without protecting the people we meant it for.
[Turn 8 ASSISTANT]
e064	You are right; I treated the channels as visitor types.
e065	Measure the path used and practical flexibility separately.
e066	Offer reliable same-day return times without eliminating immediate entry for people who cannot return.
e067	A short voluntary question can reveal the difference, but entry must not become a survey exercise.
[Turn 9 USER]
e068	The provider demonstrated the booking page.
e069	It allows one person to reserve ten free tickets, which staff fear will create empty blocks or informal resale.
e070	Requiring an account would reduce repeated reservations but conflicts with our no-account principle.
e071	The provider can cap each contact method at four tickets and send a simple confirmation request the day before.
e072	Families and small groups say four may be too low.
[Turn 9 ASSISTANT]
e073	Use a household-sized cap and a separate assisted path for larger groups rather than introducing an account solely to police scarcity.
e074	Make cancellation easy, release unconfirmed capacity gradually, and watch whether the confirmation step disproportionately removes people with limited connectivity.
e075	Free access can still require fair-use rules, but the enforcement mechanism should not create a larger barrier than the behavior it prevents.
[Turn 10 USER]
e076	The tourism office offered to place reservation links in hotel newsletters and at the airport.
e077	That could distribute demand across the day, but neighborhood organizations worry visitors will capture advance slots before residents hear about them.
e078	We do not have a resident category and do not want one.
e079	I am tempted to reject the tourism offer simply because it will make the reservation channel more successful than the assisted community block.
[Turn 10 ASSISTANT]
e080	Do not suppress tourism promotion just to balance the channels.
e081	Stagger releases, preserve walk-in and same-day capacity, and publish the same information through libraries, community partners, and the entrance.
e082	Review distribution without creating a residency test.
[Turn 11 USER]
e083	The fire marshal has now reduced safe occupancy after observing how people actually move through the exhibition.
e084	Staff say that proves timed entry is necessary.
e085	A trustee says it proves the forty-percent walk-in floor is too generous because unused reservations can always be released later.
e086	I think the second conclusion uses the safety change to protect the reservation system before it has produced evidence.
e087	Returned slots are uncertain; a walk-in floor is dependable.
e088	But I also understand that a fixed percentage means fewer total reservations now, and the outside queue could itself become a safety and weather problem.
e089	I do not want to defend forty percent because it is the number we already wrote down.
e090	I want to know whether the reason for it still holds under the new capacity.
[Turn 11 ASSISTANT]
e091	Recalculate all channel counts using the new safety limit while preserving the agreed proportion unless evidence shows it is unworkable.
e092	Returned reservations are not equivalent to dependable walk-in capacity because their timing is uncertain.
e093	If crowding creates unsafe queues outside, use same-day timed walk-in tickets and the early adjustment rule rather than quietly reallocating access before observation.
[Turn 12 USER]
e094	We will keep the forty-percent walk-in share under the revised occupancy, add same-day return times at the desk and by phone, use staggered reservation releases, and set a household-sized cap with assisted booking for larger groups.
e095	Promotion will go through tourism and neighborhood channels at the same time.
e096	We will count immediate entry, offered return times, abandoned visits, confirmations, and released capacity separately.
e097	The ten-week contract, privacy limits, weekly publication, and early walk-in adjustment remain unchanged.
[Turn 12 ASSISTANT]
e098	The final design now responds to visitor behavior rather than forcing people into “planner” and “walk-in” categories.
e099	It protects immediate access, offers reliable same-day returns, staggers advance release, and handles larger groups without requiring accounts or residency tests.
e100	It also keeps the fire marshal's safety adjustment from silently rewriting the access promise before observation.
e101	Preserve the baseline finding that many walk-ins had planned their visit, the booking-page test, confirmation losses, promotion channels, revised occupancy, outside-queue conditions, and every allocation change.
e102	The board should see who waited, who returned, who abandoned the visit, and which channel actually worked for whom—not merely whether galleries looked calmer or the reservation system filled its slots.

packet.question: What is the user's later working position, and what distinct unresolved condition, counterpressure, blind spot, or reopen reason still limits it?
packet.record_identity_contract: One record is one coherent position thread within the assigned role. Gather every material visible alias for that thread into evidence_ids. Put each distinct object or expression into a separate aligned component index inside that same record. Do not create one record per alias, sentence, object, or component. Use a second record only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread about a different subject.

role_boundary_contract.allocation: Interpret current and qualification comparatively before writing records. Allocate each meaning to the role it performs. The same source alias may support both roles only when it contains two genuinely distinct meanings; create separate role-specific components and explain the distinction. Do not duplicate one unresolved meaning into current merely because the user acknowledges it alongside the working answer.
role_boundary_contract.current: The user's later working answer: what they lean toward, propose, plan, decide, commit to, refuse, or conditionally accept, including concerns converted into adopted safeguards.
role_boundary_contract.qualification: What still limits or could reopen that answer: unresolved questions, unmet conditions, counterpressure, blind spots, side effects, or path dependence, with speaker ownership.

packet.source_coverage_contract: Review every focal alias before returning. A valid empty response is allowed only after checking both user and assistant evidence for the assigned role. Preserve later minority qualifications and counterpressure even when the current action is already clear.

prompts.system_prompt: You jointly interpret current position and whether any unresolved qualification remains after the complete endpoint. Compare roles before allocating meanings. An adopted condition, safeguard, stop rule, or reopen rule belongs to current; it is not itself unresolved. Return a qualification record only for a matter that remains unresolved and can change or reopen current. Always return a source-linked qualification_review outcome.

packet.expression_interpretation_contract: Classify expression from the source speaker's relationship to that component, not from the role name or the fact that a situation was mentioned.
